newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton heads for recovery, new arrivals low.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton heads for recovery, new arrivals low.

text.p: Indian cotton prices headed for a recovery, with prices on Monday rising on lower new arrivals and fresh mill buying, dealers said.
"New crop arrivals remained low in the producing centres as farmers were bringing in limited quantities of cotton at the lower level," one broker said.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees to 775/810 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by the same margin at 1,400/1,640 rupees per maund. F-414 was up by 20 rupees at 1,800/1,840 rupees per maund. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) lifted by 200/300 rupees to 11,300/11,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
Arrivals in the Punjab region fell on Monday to 10,000/12,000 bales (170 kg each) against a daily average of 20,000/25,000 bales last week.
